units.title: Bootstrap the engine repository and durable project record
units.acceptanceCriteria: A fresh checkout builds the minimal SDK and example with documented commands. Every planned card has an ID, owner lane, dependency and truthful planned status; repository ownership and distribution policy are recorded.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Create the engine workspace, package/service boundaries, local commands, architecture decision directory, development plan, handoff record and machine-readable progress ledger. Reserve interface packages for consumers and examples without conference imports.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run the clean-checkout build and package import smoke check; validate progress schema and reject application imports in engine packages.
sourceMetadata.security: Exclude credentials and source assets from accidental publication. Record dependency trust boundaries and repository protection settings.

units.title: Establish CI evidence and the merge procedure
units.acceptanceCriteria: A deliberately failing required check blocks acceptance. A changed commit invalidates prior review/check evidence. Progress distinguishes implemented, verified, merged, deployed and release-qualified work.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Add scoped build, unit, integration, browser, migration and security jobs, shared fixtures, artifact retention and a reproducible acceptance record keyed to commit and environment. Document separate self security review followed by required checks and merge verification.
sourceMetadata.tests: Exercise passing and failing workflow fixtures, stale-evidence rejection, test sharding and deterministic artifact naming.
sourceMetadata.security: Use minimal workflow permissions, pinned actions and secret redaction; untrusted pull-request code cannot receive deployment credentials.

units.title: Define shared contracts and qualification fixtures
units.acceptanceCriteria: The same fixtures and scripted interactions can run against either candidate foundation. Thresholds, feature requirements and evidence formats are fixed before comparative results are reviewed.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Define versioned runtime, asset, world, media, identity and service interface contracts. Select canonical meters/axes and prepare test architecture, animated creature, screens, movable props and four audio corners. Establish reference device and workload manifests.
sourceMetadata.tests: Validate manifests, schema compatibility fixtures, coordinate transforms and scripted scenario reproducibility.
sourceMetadata.security: Use redistributable synthetic fixtures for CI and protect privately obtained originals in controlled test storage; fixture provenance does not constrain product import capabilities.

units.title: Qualify Hubs and Spoke as a complete foundation
externalPrerequisites: An actual target headset for comparative XR evidence
units.acceptanceCriteria: Publish runnable evidence against F03 requirements, an extraction/deployment assessment and concrete adaptation estimates. Feature claims without exercised behavior remain unverified.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Build a reproducible Hubs/Spoke evaluation branch or isolated package using pinned sources. Exercise imported venue, avatar, object manipulation, shared media, browser editing, export/reload and headset entry; record components retained and required changes.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run the common desktop/two-client scenario and actual-headset checklist; capture frame timing and reconnect behavior without claiming production capacity.
sourceMetadata.security: Inventory covered licenses, exposed services, default access policies and stale dependencies; document necessary patches rather than imposing marketplace feature restrictions.

units.title: Qualify Babylon and reusable VRSpace subsystems
externalPrerequisites: An actual target headset for comparative XR evidence
units.acceptanceCriteria: The evidence is directly comparable with F04. The proposed combination demonstrates the critical interactions and identifies functionality still requiring implementation.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Build the equivalent F03 evaluation using Babylon and candidate VRSpace client subsystems. Test scene authoring, avatars, media surfaces, spatial audio, physics integration and portable world state. Record reusable modules and server coupling.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run the same desktop, multi-client and headset scenarios; inspect bundle size, frame cost and service boundaries.
sourceMetadata.security: Check client/server separation, dependency notices, untrusted media routes and credential handling. Do not import an entire service stack merely to obtain a small client module.

units.title: Select the foundation and map retained subsystems
units.acceptanceCriteria: All required outcomes remain assigned. A Hubs selection may retain its working networking/media/editor systems; it does not force replacement by the default libraries. Reused functionality closes a card only after its acceptance checks pass.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Record the foundation decision against capability coverage, adaptation effort, graphics, operations and maintainability. Map every remaining card to reuse, adapt or implement. Keep one runtime foundation; retire the losing production path while retaining its evaluation evidence.
sourceMetadata.tests: Validate the capability mapping, full dependency graph and a build of the selected foundation.
sourceMetadata.security: Document software obligations and patch ownership. Preserve full import, editing and export goals and an application-independent engine boundary.

units.title: Pin upstream components and establish fork maintenance
units.acceptanceCriteria: A clean build resolves the recorded dependency set and can identify the source of every shipped binary. Local modifications have a reproducible patch or branch history.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Create only necessary source forks; otherwise pin upstream packages and service images. Record source versions, patches, notices, software bill of materials and update responsibilities. Define regression checks for upstream upgrades and supported toolchain versions.
sourceMetadata.tests: Rebuild from lockfiles and verify artifact provenance, license inventory and an example dependency update/revert.
sourceMetadata.security: Review build scripts, supply-chain exposure and distribution obligations, including native converter builds. No secret or private asset enters a package by default.

units.title: Establish the engine control API and data services
units.acceptanceCriteria: A standalone host can create a scoped workspace and call engine APIs without conference records. Two tenants cannot access each other; retries preserve one result and failed migrations recover predictably.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Implement host-injected identity, tenant/project namespaces, scoped capabilities and basic control API middleware. Add durable schema migrations, object-store/queue interfaces, idempotent job contracts and a local service stack. Keep product roles in the host application.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run real database, object-store and queue integration tests plus authorization, token expiry, migration rollback/forward and idempotency cases.
sourceMetadata.security: Apply transport encryption, secret isolation, least-privilege service grants and explicit processing trust boundaries; do not claim participant-held encryption for server-readable simulation data.

units.title: Version complete world, entity and prefab schemas
units.acceptanceCriteria: A fixture containing nested prefabs, negative scales, media references and behavior data validates and round-trips without losing identity. Unknown optional components survive preservation; unsupported required components produce actionable errors. Meters, right-handed axes and Y-up remain invariant.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Extend foundation contracts into versioned world, entity, prefab and asset-reference schemas, including component extension points, stable identifiers, hierarchy, source coordinates and migration hooks. Map the selected foundation into these contracts instead of introducing a second scene model.
sourceMetadata.tests: Exercise malformed references, parent cycles, duplicate identifiers, schema migration and coordinate round-trips against independent fixtures.
sourceMetadata.security: Bound nesting, component sizes and numeric ranges; reject prototype-polluting keys and unresolved external references before instantiation.

units.title: Implement runtime lifecycle and injectable local services
units.acceptanceCriteria: A minimal world starts without a conference account, application API or media server. Loading another world cancels obsolete work and disposes previous resources. Repeated mount/unmount and suspended-tab recovery leave one active frame loop and consistent lifecycle events.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Expose create, load, start, suspend, resume, unload and dispose operations around the chosen runtime. Provide injectable asset, authorization, persistence and transport interfaces with local implementations. Separate scene state from rendering resources and host application UI.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run lifecycle integration tests covering cancellation, failed loads, late asynchronous results and repeated mounting; inspect retained resource counts.
sourceMetadata.security: Local mode grants only its explicit local capabilities; absent host authorization must never silently authorize a remote world.

units.title: Load canonical assets into the selected renderer
units.acceptanceCriteria: The reference scene loads meshes, textures, lights and animation clips with preserved transforms and source diagnostics. Repeated instances share eligible resources, while disposing one instance leaves others intact. Required unsupported features fail visibly instead of silently disappearing.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Connect published asset manifests to the selected renderer, reusing its glTF, material, lighting, animation and texture facilities. Support dependency resolution, loading placeholders, cancellation, shared-resource ownership and documented advanced renderer extensions without rebuilding the upstream rendering pipeline.
sourceMetadata.tests: Compare representative render fixtures and test missing textures, corrupt resources, cancelled loads, negative scales and shared-resource disposal.
sourceMetadata.security: Load only authorized manifest resources; enforce resource ceilings and prevent renderer plugins from fetching arbitrary asset URLs.

units.title: Provide desktop, touch and accessible action input
units.acceptanceCriteria: Users navigate and select objects with desktop or touch controls without triggering movement while typing. Pointer-lock refusal, focus loss, orientation changes and device disconnection recover predictably. Host UI can consume an action without depending on renderer internals or conference roles.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Add application-neutral action bindings for movement, look, selection, interaction and cancellation across keyboard, mouse, touch and gamepad. Provide remapping, focus ownership, pointer-lock lifecycle and accessible equivalents for essential non-spatial controls.
sourceMetadata.tests: Use browser interaction tests for input capture, remapping, focus transitions, touch gestures and stuck-key prevention; verify keyboard-only operation manually.
sourceMetadata.security: Validate incoming synthetic actions through the same bounded action contract; user gestures cannot bypass remote permissions or object capabilities.

units.title: Integrate WebXR sessions, controllers and comfort controls
externalPrerequisites: Physical WebXR headset and controllers for acceptance.
units.acceptanceCriteria: Capability detection exposes only available entry modes. A supported headset enters, exits, recenters and resumes without duplicate inputs or displaced world scale. Session denial and controller loss return usable controls. Locomotion requests remain subject to later collision and authority validation.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Adapt the selected foundation's WebXR session and controller support into shared input actions, reference-space handling and session lifecycle. Implement snap turning, teleport requests, seated/recenter controls and optional smooth locomotion with explicit comfort settings.
sourceMetadata.tests: Combine mocked session/error tests with recorded physical-headset checks for controller profiles, reference-space resets, sleep/resume and comfort settings.
sourceMetadata.security: Tracking stays ephemeral by default; XR availability never grants movement, editing or media capabilities.

units.title: Add VR-safe controls and qualified hand interaction
externalPrerequisites: Qualified hand-tracking headset for the advertised hand profile.
units.acceptanceCriteria: Users can dismiss errors, adjust comfort, select objects and leave the session inside the headset. Essential controls do not depend on invisible HTML overlays. Hand/controller switching does not duplicate activation, and unsupported tracking preserves a complete interaction route.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Provide reusable XR panels, readable prompts, focus states and interaction targets for controller rays and direct selection. Add hand-tracking adaptation where supported, with pinch/debounce handling and controller or desktop fallback; reuse qualified upstream UI components.
sourceMetadata.tests: Test focus and action routing automatically; verify target reach, text legibility, hand occlusion, accidental pinches and device switching on actual hardware.
sourceMetadata.security: UI visibility is independent of authority; repeated or spoofed activations still pass object capability and rate checks.

units.title: Bridge collision assets and fixed-step physics
units.acceptanceCriteria: Architectural openings remain traversable while floors and walls are solid. Physics owns simulated transforms; rendering interpolates without altering authority. Repeated loads release bodies and shapes. Fixed-step behavior is bounded under frame stalls without claiming universal cross-platform deterministic lockstep.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Implement the selected physics bridge, defaulting to Rapier, for static, kinematic and dynamic bodies, collider manifests, mass properties, collision filters, contacts and transform interpolation. Expose a headless simulation interface suitable for local and authoritative hosting. Use independent collider fixtures first; A13 subsequently supplies production-derived geometry.
sourceMetadata.tests: Exercise stairs, arches, negative-scale assets, thin barriers, falling bodies, contact events and frame stalls using independent geometry fixtures.
sourceMetadata.security: Reject malformed collider data, excessive body counts, invalid numeric values and unbounded catch-up simulation.

units.title: Implement character traversal, seating and safe teleportation
externalPrerequisites: Physical headset for tracked-camera boundary and seating acceptance.
units.acceptanceCriteria: The traversal fixture supports stairs, ramps, doorways and moving platforms without falling through unloaded collision. Invalid teleports fail clearly. Removing a floor triggers a safe recovery. Real head movement remains tracked; boundary feedback handles wall penetration without forcibly moving the camera.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Build a capsule-based character controller with walking, slopes, steps, ground detection, seating, configurable participant collision and validated teleport destinations. Connect shared input and comfort actions while keeping tracked headset motion distinct from virtual body constraints.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run reproducible traversal scenarios plus headset checks for seated scale, recentering, wall approach and interrupted teleport requests.
sourceMetadata.security: Bound speed, acceleration, teleport range and spawn choices; authoritative validation can replay the same movement intent contract.

units.title: Implement object manipulation, throwing and joints
units.acceptanceCriteria: A statue can be carried, placed or thrown with predictable release velocity and collisions. Jointed doors obey limits. Losing input, deleting an object or suspending a session releases control safely. The same command/result contract can be hosted by the network authority.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Define reusable interaction intents and control-lease state for selecting, grabbing, carrying, placing and throwing dynamic objects. Implement local physics constraints and bounded joints for doors, levers and attached props, using desktop and XR interaction adapters.
sourceMetadata.tests: Exercise heavy/light props, fast release, collision during grabs, joint limits, simultaneous local requests and interrupted interactions.
sourceMetadata.security: Enforce interaction distance, object capability, force and velocity ceilings; imported properties cannot create unlimited constraints.

units.title: Connect physics interactions to room authority
units.acceptanceCriteria: Two clients contesting one object receive one valid owner. Late joiners see current poses, joints and control state. Packet delay, duplicate messages and disconnects produce bounded correction and lease release. A client cannot tunnel, teleport or launch objects by submitting unchecked transforms.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Bind movement and manipulation intents to the authoritative room service with lease arbitration, acknowledgments, local prediction, correction and remote interpolation. Reuse the selected networking primitives; keep shared body ownership separate from collaborative document state.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run two-client browser scenarios and headless fault tests for delayed commands, stale leases, replayed releases and prediction reconciliation.
sourceMetadata.security: Review all client-controlled movement fields; validate principal, instance epoch, object scope and replay handling before accepting state changes.

units.title: Integrate navigation meshes, routes and world transitions
units.acceptanceCriteria: Routes pass through real doorways and avoid blocked or unloaded regions. A removed bridge invalidates affected paths and safe spawn recovery works. A portal resolves a destination without assuming conference sessions; remote authorization and transition orchestration remain host-service responsibilities.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Integrate Recast/Detour or the qualified reused navigation subsystem for tiled walkability, path queries, off-mesh connections, NPC routing and portal destination contracts. Invalidate impacted navigation regions when geometry changes and expose rebuild status to the runtime.
sourceMetadata.tests: Compare paths against independent obstacle fixtures; exercise disconnected islands, stale tiles, moved blockers and cancellation during transitions.
sourceMetadata.security: Bound pathfinding work and destination requests; reject unauthorized destination references and malformed navigation links.

units.title: Load generic avatars and a qualified VRM adapter
units.acceptanceCriteria: Multiple independently sourced fixture avatars load at correct scale with stable bone references and valid bounds. Unsupported rigs return useful diagnostics or a safe placeholder. Replacing an avatar disposes resources without changing participant identity or losing host capabilities.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Create an avatar resource contract for skinned glTF, morph targets, skeleton mappings, body bounds and attachment sockets. Adapt VRM where qualified and preserve unsupported metadata for export. Reuse existing avatar loading rather than imposing one hosted avatar vendor.
sourceMetadata.tests: Cover differing bone names, absent optional bones, morph targets, oversized skeletons, malformed skin indices and repeated avatar replacement.
sourceMetadata.security: Enforce texture, bone, morph and material budgets; avatar metadata and extensions must not execute embedded code.

units.title: Add avatar animation, retargeting and emote playback
units.acceptanceCriteria: Compatible fixture rigs play walking, seated transitions and several emotes without scale drift or losing foot contact beyond the agreed tolerance. Unsupported retarget mappings are reported. Interrupting an emote returns smoothly to locomotion; root motion never bypasses the physics controller.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Provide animation state machines, clip libraries, blending, root-motion policy and qualified skeleton retargeting. Define generic locomotion, seating, gestures and emote actions with authored fallback mappings rather than assuming every humanoid shares one rig.
sourceMetadata.tests: Check clip transitions, missing clips, loop boundaries, different frame rates, root offsets and retargeted reference poses.
sourceMetadata.security: Bound animation events and clip resource use; event markers invoke approved actions instead of arbitrary code or privileged commands.

units.title: Add avatar presence, inverse kinematics and attachments
externalPrerequisites: Physical headset for head/hand calibration and optional tracking claims.
units.acceptanceCriteria: An avatar follows tracked head/hands at the configured scale, while absent tracking produces a stable fallback rather than invented measured poses. Attachments remain aligned through animation and avatar replacement. Local and remote pose contracts distinguish tracked, estimated and unavailable data.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Map available head and hand poses onto avatar bones using qualified inverse kinematics, calibration and bounded fallback poses. Add wearable/held attachment sockets, local source offsets and capability adapters for optional face/body tracking without requiring that hardware.
sourceMetadata.tests: Exercise seated calibration, tracking loss, arm reach limits, controller changes and attachment motion on fixture rigs and hardware.
sourceMetadata.security: Minimize tracking retention and bound pose updates; attachment assets retain ordinary ownership and resource restrictions.

units.title: Implement animated wildlife and reusable NPC behaviors
externalPrerequisites: A usable rigged animal asset for the final fidelity check.
units.acceptanceCriteria: A rigged bird follows a route, changes clips and carries its sound emitter without requiring human bone names. Lower-detail clients preserve its authoritative location and behavior. Missing optional audio or clips produces a documented fallback; authored routes stay within configured bounds.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Add reusable path-following, flying-route, idle and scheduled-behavior components for non-humanoid actors. Bind imported clips, simple interaction bounds and entity-attached audio while separating shared behavior timing from locally evaluated skeletal animation.
sourceMetadata.tests: Use synthetic animal fixtures for clip timing, route loops and LOD changes; inspect one actual animated wildlife asset before claiming fidelity.
sourceMetadata.security: Cap active actors, route complexity and event frequency; decorative actors cannot acquire participant or editor privileges.

units.title: Add terrain tiles and environmental scene components
units.acceptanceCriteria: A tiled landscape loads without visible or physical cracks at approved borders. Terrain edits invalidate affected collision/navigation revisions before traversal resumes. Water and weather have lower-cost fallbacks, and disabling decorative effects leaves navigation and world state unchanged.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Implement versioned terrain tiles, heightfield/mesh rendering and collision bindings, plus reusable sky, water and bounded weather components. Reuse renderer facilities and material presets; keep environmental simulation and quality policy independent of conference venue themes.
sourceMetadata.tests: Exercise neighboring tile seams, origin/scale conversions, terrain replacement, unloaded boundaries and reduced-effects rendering against reference fixtures.
sourceMetadata.security: Bound tile size, update frequency, particle counts and environmental parameters; malformed height data cannot exhaust memory or destabilize simulation.

units.title: Provide declarative object behaviors and trusted extensions
units.acceptanceCriteria: A fixture game uses interaction, timed events and state transitions without conference code. Behaviors run in the correct local or authoritative context, survive save/reload and handle entity deletion. Cyclic trigger graphs stop at declared execution budgets with useful diagnostics.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Implement versioned triggers, conditions, timers and approved actions for doors, exhibits, object interaction and simple games. Supply a documented trusted-plugin interface and renderer escape hatch while preserving behavior metadata in the world manifest.
sourceMetadata.tests: Exercise event ordering, timer cancellation, graph cycles, missing action providers and replay after restoring a world revision.
sourceMetadata.security: Authorize every privileged action, constrain event amplification and keep imported script text inert unless an explicitly supported runtime admits it.

units.title: Qualify and integrate isolated creator scripting
units.acceptanceCriteria: A creator-authored object performs useful logic through approved APIs and survives revision export/reload. Infinite loops, excessive allocation and unauthorized host calls terminate without taking down the world. Browser/server differences are explicit; a worker alone is not accepted as isolation.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Select and integrate an isolated creator-code runtime with an explicit capability bridge, bounded execution, controlled storage/network access and termination, plus an optional browser script-editor panel. Keep trusted engine plugins separate. Document supported language/runtime versions, execution locations and serialization of script state.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run adversarial scripts, cancellation, upgrade compatibility and capability-revocation cases in the actual selected isolation mechanism.
sourceMetadata.security: Complete a separate escape/broker review covering ambient credentials, origin access, imports, resource ceilings and authoritative command validation.

units.title: Implement scene streaming and adaptive quality budgets
units.acceptanceCriteria: A low-power profile reduces decorative detail while preserving presentation readability, authoritative geometry and usable movement. Collision arrives before entry into streamed regions. Repeated quality changes do not oscillate, leak assets or duplicate entities; premium source variants remain available.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Connect asset variants and spatial cells to projected-size LOD, culling, instancing, staged loading and bounded animation updates. Add separate rendering, memory, transfer and decode budgets with manual quality settings, downgrade hysteresis and gradual recovery.
sourceMetadata.tests: Replay representative camera routes under bandwidth and frame-load limits; inspect resource counts, variant selection and collision-before-traversal ordering.
sourceMetadata.security: Enforce world and client budgets despite hostile asset metadata; quality selection must not bypass content authorization.

units.title: Harden renderer selection and graphics recovery
externalPrerequisites: Actual target browsers and headsets for each advertised backend profile.
units.acceptanceCriteria: Unsupported XR/backend combinations offer a working fallback before entry or reconstruct predictably. Simulated context loss restores the current world without duplicate physics or audio. Failed restoration exposes a recoverable user action while preserving independent meeting connections where possible.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Implement capability-based backend selection and recovery around the chosen foundation: conservative WebGL2 immersive entry, qualified WebGPU paths and controlled scene reconstruction. Handle context/device loss without conflating graphics resources with world state or media connections.
sourceMetadata.tests: Exercise capability matrices, denied sessions, resource recreation, backend changes, headset sleep and repeated device/context loss on supported profiles.
sourceMetadata.security: Recreated resources recheck authorized manifests; recovery cannot revive revoked assets, stale grants or superseded world instances.

units.title: Ship independent offline and multiplayer game examples
units.acceptanceCriteria: The offline example works with network access disabled after its packaged assets load. The multiplayer example joins an engine world service directly and supports two interacting clients. Both examples use the same contracts and document deployment/configuration without hidden conference dependencies.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Publish a local physics playground and a small multiplayer game using only released engine interfaces. Demonstrate loading, movement, collision, object rules, reset/save and host-provided identity without importing conference routes, account models, agendas or presenter roles.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run import-boundary checks, offline browser tests and a two-client game flow including save/reset and reconnection.
sourceMetadata.security: Use explicit demonstration permissions; sample credentials and permissive development settings must not enter published production defaults.

units.title: Qualify runtime performance and supported device profiles
externalPrerequisites: Reference laptops/headsets and approved representative venue/animal assets.
units.acceptanceCriteria: Each advertised profile sustains its selected desktop or headset target and preserves traversal, essential controls and readable presentations. Low-quality fallbacks and graphics recovery work during active media. Failures narrow the published claim and produce corrective work before that profile is accepted.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Run integrated runtime qualification with representative venues, actors, avatars and media. Publish supported device/backend profiles, reproducible scene versions, p95/p99 frame timings, memory/decoder observations and outstanding fidelity limits rather than one unqualified frame-rate claim.
sourceMetadata.tests: Replay camera/interaction workloads on actual laptops and headsets, varying active avatars, animals, screens and network conditions independently.
sourceMetadata.security: Review telemetry for sensitive tracking/media leakage and confirm resource ceilings remain effective during overload and recovery.

units.title: Implement persistent inventories and object ownership
units.acceptanceCriteria: A player can collect, carry, store, equip and re-place an object across reconnects without duplicating its identity. Shared venue props and personal items follow distinct ownership rules and remain usable by non-conference examples.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Add application-neutral inventories, object ownership, prefab instances, pickup/stow/drop operations and equipment/attachment slots. Persist item identity separately from shared render assets and connect state changes to authoritative capabilities and revisions.
sourceMetadata.tests: Test concurrent pickup, reconnect during transfer, duplicate retries, destroyed items, attachment replacement and persistence restoration.
sourceMetadata.security: Check item, inventory and world capabilities at every transfer; clients cannot mint items, seize another inventory or export private dependencies by changing ownership metadata.

units.title: Asset revisions, preserved sources and converter contracts
units.acceptanceCriteria: An uploaded source receives a stable revision and can be retrieved byte-for-byte after a derived revision changes. Capability declarations distinguish native import, exchange import and export without marketplace-specific feature restrictions.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Define versioned asset, source-bundle, dependency, conversion-recipe and diagnostic schemas. Register importer/exporter adapters with explicit format, version and feature declarations. Preserve original bytes, companion files, authoring coordinates, names, pivots and hashes independently of derived runtime outputs. Provide application-neutral catalog and operation contracts.
sourceMetadata.tests: Round-trip schema fixtures, malformed dependency graphs, source-hash verification and recipe-version migration prove identity preservation and compatibility failures.
sourceMetadata.security: Check tenant ownership on every source, dependency and revision operation; reject ambient filesystem references.

units.title: Resumable intake for files, folders and archives
units.acceptanceCriteria: A network interruption resumes verified chunks without restarting the complete upload. Folder and archive submissions retain equivalent dependency paths, and canceling removes only the intended incomplete session. Unsupported archive types produce actionable results.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Implement browser and API intake for individual files, folder selections, drag-and-drop directories and supported archives. Stage a dependency bundle with relative paths, checksums, multipart/resumable progress, cancellation and expiration. Preserve companion textures and nested directories; identify archives by signatures rather than extensions.
sourceMetadata.tests: Exercise interrupted and repeated completion, duplicate filenames in different folders, Unicode paths, mobile file selection, oversized entries and corrupt chunk hashes.
sourceMetadata.security: Bind upload tokens to one tenant/session; enforce quotas, path containment, bounded entry counts and safe archive expansion limits.

units.title: Isolated conversion jobs and recoverable execution
units.acceptanceCriteria: A real conversion job survives worker loss through a safe retry and publishes at most one result. A canceled or timed-out job stops its subprocesses, releases its lease and leaves original data intact.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Run pinned converters in disposable workers with durable jobs, leases, checkpoints where supported, cancellation, bounded retries and structured progress. Separate staged sources from writable outputs. Record actual tool versions and build inventories. Implement process termination, cleanup and terminal failure classification.
sourceMetadata.tests: Kill workers before and after output commit; inject queue redelivery, disk exhaustion, malformed parser input and converter hangs. Verify resource accounting and cleanup.
sourceMetadata.security: Use nonprivileged isolation, no ambient credentials, restricted filesystem/network access and CPU, memory, disk and wall-time limits.

units.title: Canonical glTF and GLB ingestion with feature validation
units.acceptanceCriteria: Representative static and animated fixtures render with correct scale, orientation, hierarchy and materials. Required unsupported extensions prevent a false success; optional approximations remain visible in diagnostics. A valid small GLB can preview before hosted optimization finishes.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Implement glTF/GLB loading through the selected runtime and canonical compiler path. Validate buffers, references, skins, clips, morph targets, materials and supported extensions. Normalize source coordinates once while retaining original conventions and stable sub-object identifiers. Publish an explicit extension/fidelity matrix.
sourceMetadata.tests: Use Khronos fixtures plus mirrored transforms, interleaved buffers, sparse accessors, missing textures, invalid numeric values and oversized allocations; compare rendered reference views.
sourceMetadata.security: Bound decoded resources and resolve only authorized bundle dependencies; never execute asset-provided code.

units.title: Immutable publication, reusable results and asset lifecycle
units.acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent identical jobs converge on one valid published result; changing any meaningful recipe input creates a distinct revision. Worlds remain pinned to their selected assets. Unreferenced outputs can be reclaimed without deleting active world or export dependencies.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Publish immutable manifests and derivative objects atomically, keyed by source hashes, tool versions and complete recipes. Add catalog lookup, asynchronous job-result retrieval, CDN delivery, original retrieval endpoints and reference-aware lifecycle management. Support rebuilding with new recipes without rewriting older worlds.
sourceMetadata.tests: Exercise interrupted publication, duplicate completion, cache invalidation, expired delivery grants, concurrent references, deletion races and restoration from retained originals.
sourceMetadata.security: Authorize every catalog and byte-delivery request; prevent cross-tenant existence leaks and unsafe shared-cache keys.

units.title: OBJ, MTL, COLLADA and legacy 3DS conversion
units.acceptanceCriteria: A folder containing an architectural OBJ, its MTL and textures becomes an editable runtime asset. A DAE venue retains its hierarchy and openings. Missing dependencies produce specific repair instructions, and static OBJ never claims to preserve skeletal animation.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Add qualified OBJ/MTL, DAE and legacy .3ds adapters using pinned open-source tools. Preserve supported geometry, object grouping, transforms, texture references and basic material properties. Record tested exporter variants and supported animation features. Keep .3ds distinct from native .max scenes.
sourceMetadata.tests: Convert exporter-diverse fixtures with relative texture paths, negative scale, differing units, transparency, large indices and unsupported DAE features; inspect reference renders.
sourceMetadata.security: Disable XML external entities and reject escaped paths, excessive nesting and unbounded material/mesh counts.

units.title: FBX meshes, skins, morphs and animation clips
units.acceptanceCriteria: Binary and ASCII FBX fixtures load as the same animated characters at representative poses. Clip names and duration survive conversion, and a file needing native baking cannot silently become a static success.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Qualify ufbx and the selected Blender route against the same corpus, then implement the better supported FBX adapter. Preserve hierarchy, units, pivots, skins, blend shapes, clip ranges and supported material bindings. Report constraints, expressions or shader features that require evaluation in the source application.
sourceMetadata.tests: Compare skinned poses, morph weights, inverse bind transforms, loop seams, reflected coordinates and multiple animation takes against exported references. Include malformed and truncated FBX inputs.
sourceMetadata.security: Use isolated parsing with allocation limits; embedded media and external references remain within the authorized source bundle.

units.title: Native Blender scene conversion
units.acceptanceCriteria: Supported .blend scenes produce editable runtime assets with correct objects, clips and appearance. Sources requiring missing libraries or unsafe embedded execution report the issue without losing originals or automatically enabling scripts.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Implement a version-qualified headless Blender adapter for .blend sources using trusted pipeline scripts. Resolve bundled textures and linked libraries, preserve supported geometry and animation, and identify unsupported node, modifier or driver behavior. Record the exact Blender build and conversion settings in every result.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run real Blender conversions covering packed/unpacked textures, linked assets, modifiers, geometry nodes within the supported subset and animations; compare outputs and expected failure diagnostics.
sourceMetadata.security: Disable embedded autoexecution, isolate subprocesses and limit dependency resolution; inventory distributed Blender scripts and binaries.

units.title: USD family composition and conversion
units.acceptanceCriteria: A packaged USD scene with local references converts reproducibly using an explicit variant selection. Missing payloads and unsupported curves, volumes or materials appear as identified issues rather than an apparently complete empty asset.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Add version-qualified USD, USDA, USDC and USDZ intake through Blender/OpenUSD tools. Resolve declared references, payloads and selected variants within the source bundle; convert the documented mesh, hierarchy, material and animation subset. Preserve source composition metadata and report every unsupported semantic.
sourceMetadata.tests: Compare composed transforms, instancing, selected variants, time samples and material references against native source inspection; exercise broken references, cycles and archive faults.
sourceMetadata.security: Block arbitrary filesystem or network resolution and custom resolver/plugin execution; bound composition depth and expanded resource size.

units.title: STL, PLY and 3MF geometry classification
units.acceptanceCriteria: Ordinary geometry imports at the chosen physical scale with preserved supported colors and assemblies. A splat or point file is never misreported as a broken triangle mesh. Users can inspect and correct unknown-unit assumptions before placement.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Implement tested STL, mesh-PLY and 3MF conversion with geometry, color, assembly and unit handling appropriate to each format. Classify point-cloud and Gaussian-splat PLY schemas explicitly and dispatch them to their specialized adapter status. Offer scale calibration when the source omits units.
sourceMetadata.tests: Use ASCII/binary STL and PLY, colored meshes, 3MF assemblies, mixed-schema PLY, degenerate faces, missing units and malformed container relationships.
sourceMetadata.security: Apply shared archive containment, XML safety and decoded vertex/face limits; reject nonfinite coordinates and oversized declared counts.

units.title: Material and animation baking with fidelity reports
units.acceptanceCriteria: Procedural fixtures within the supported subset produce stable PBR outputs and animated clips. Unsupported renderer or rig features produce a correction-required result; static exchange geometry never substitutes silently for a promised animated asset.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Build shared baking recipes for supported materials, UV preparation, textures, animation resampling, skin/morph outputs and named clips. Separate source evaluation from runtime encoding so native connectors can contribute evaluated data later. Preserve original high-quality assets and record approximations, missing renderers and deformation losses.
sourceMetadata.tests: Compare reference views, UV seams, normal orientation, feather silhouettes, clip endpoints, morph deformation and baked transform poses using real supported toolchains.
sourceMetadata.security: Execute only trusted recipes; imported expressions or scripts cannot run outside qualified isolated source-application evaluation.

units.title: Mesh, texture, LOD and spatial-cell optimization
units.acceptanceCriteria: A large venue streams nearby cells and appropriate LODs without loading its full detail first. Animated assets retain valid skins and clips across tiers. High-quality sources remain available, and all rendering variants refer to the same authoritative object locations.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Generate device-tier derivatives using glTF Transform, meshoptimizer and KTX/Basis tooling. Separate byte compression, mesh simplification, texture resizing, material consolidation, instancing and spatial partitioning. Preserve artist-provided LODs and stable entity/sub-object mappings; record recipe-specific resource and quality statistics.
sourceMetadata.tests: Measure transfer, decoded memory, draw calls, geometric error, texture artifacts, LOD transitions and animation deformation on fixed fixtures; prove cache invalidation when recipes change.
sourceMetadata.security: Cap expansion and optimization work; validate compressed outputs and prevent shared-buffer corruption or oversized GPU allocations.

units.title: Derived colliders, navigation and safe placement data
units.acceptanceCriteria: The reference venue remains traversable without passing through walls or enclosing its interior in one convex hull. A throwable statue uses stable bounded collision geometry. Collision readiness is distinct from visual readiness for streamed cells.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Generate separate collision and navigation artifacts from normalized geometry. Use simplified static meshes or suitable primitives for venues, bounded convex compounds for movable props, and authored overrides where needed. Preserve doorways, arches and courtyards; produce walkable areas, teleport surfaces, interaction bounds and safe spawn candidates.
sourceMetadata.tests: Exercise doorway clearance, stairs, thin floors, concave props, mirrored scale, missing geometry and collider simplification error through the reference controller and physics adapter.
sourceMetadata.security: Enforce collider complexity and decomposition time limits; reject unsafe spawn data and unbounded navigation generation.

units.title: Unified browser import, diagnostics and preview workflow
units.acceptanceCriteria: A user drops a venue, sees truthful progress, checks scale and traversal, then places repeated props. Ready GLBs preview quickly; large scenes remain usable while processing. Failed or canceled imports leave no ghost scene entities or lost originals.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Connect the shared drop target to editor placement, immediate placeholders, progress, cancellation, preview generation and repairable diagnostics. Display detected formats, units, missing dependencies, clip/material coverage and resource estimates. Support replacing dependencies and rerunning a recipe without duplicating the intended object. Integrate A25 remote URL sources into the same import progress, diagnostics and publication flow.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run desktop and supported headset upload/placement flows, reconnect during processing, cancel/delete races, dependency repair and repeated completion events; compare thumbnails with runtime output.
sourceMetadata.security: Authorize import-to-world attachment separately from upload; sanitize diagnostics, filenames and preview metadata shown in the browser.

units.title: Original retrieval and interoperable scene export
units.acceptanceCriteria: Users retrieve identical originals and export editable supported geometry, materials and animation without supplier-specific product restrictions. Reimported exchange files preserve their documented subset; engine-only behaviors are identified for complete-bundle export.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Expose complete original-bundle retrieval and an export adapter registry with GLB/glTF and a documented OBJ subset. Export selected objects or supported scene snapshots with stable metadata sidecars and explicit feature-loss reports. Document and test foreign-engine exchange-export intake without treating native project containers or scripts as interchange.
sourceMetadata.tests: Reimport exported scenes in this engine and an independent compatible viewer; verify transforms, names, materials, skins and clips. Exercise foreign-engine-produced exchange fixtures.
sourceMetadata.security: Check export scope and dependency access; strip session credentials and never execute source-project scripts during intake.

units.title: Complete world bundles and editable round trips
units.acceptanceCriteria: An exported world opens in a clean workspace with preserved stable IDs, editable relationships and essential behaviors. Clone mode remaps references consistently. Live credentials are replaced by explicit reconnect requirements, while file-backed content remains portable.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Export and reimport versioned world bundles containing the manifest, dependency graph, assets, optional originals, terrain, prefabs, colliders, navigation, behaviors, media/audio bindings and revision metadata. Provide explicit portable-source inclusion and external-media references. Implement schema migration, collision-safe clone mapping and transactional import.
sourceMetadata.tests: Compare semantic snapshots and interactive behavior after export/reimport; exercise migrations, missing dependencies, duplicate IDs, partial upload and rollback after late validation failure.
sourceMetadata.security: Verify bundle integrity and access scope; treat imported behaviors as untrusted data until the behavior system authorizes activation.

units.title: Qualified native SketchUp connector
externalPrerequisites: Provisioned SketchUp SDK/application access and supported deployment rights; real native fixtures are required for acceptance.
units.acceptanceCriteria: Real SKP fixtures convert through the deployed native toolchain and compare correctly with source views. A DAE workaround or mocked connector cannot mark native SKP import accepted. Unavailable native software reports its provisioning dependency accurately.

sourceMetadata.deliverable: Implement a version-qualified SKP connector using an actually provisioned supported native SDK or application route. Preserve geometry, components, instance transforms, materials and dependency metadata within the declared subset. Expose qualified native export capabilities through the adapter registry; keep DAE exchange as an independent usable route.
sourceMetadata.tests: Run native component, nested-instance, texture, units and version fixtures; exercise actual process failure and unsupported source-version diagnostics.
sourceMetadata.security: Isolate native execution and validate source dependencies and generated output.

units.title: Qualified native Maya rig and scene connector
